title: Desktop theme that follows the OS
when: The desktop app should match the OS light or dark mode live, honor high contrast settings and feel native next to other apps.
inputs: manual theme choice needed or not
prompt:
Goal: Theme tokens that switch live with the OS, a System, Light, Dark setting, and support for forced colors high contrast mode.
Steps:
1. :root { color-scheme: light dark; } with tokens --bg, --panel, --text, --muted, --accent, --border, --focus.
2. Dark values in @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark), overridden by [data-theme="light"] or [data-theme="dark"] on html when the user picks one.
3. theme.js applies the setting at start before first paint and listens to matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)") change events while the choice is System.
4. Use system fonts: font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; and the accent keyword AccentColor where supported, with a token fallback.
5. @media (forced-colors: active): drop custom backgrounds on controls, use CanvasText, ButtonText and Highlight keywords, keep borders visible.
6. Native parts (title bar, dialogs, tray) follow the OS on their own; keep the in window header color close to them.
7. Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) to turn off theme transition animations.
Quality bar:
- Switching the OS theme updates the open window within a second.
- Text contrast is 4.5 to 1 in both themes.
Pitfalls:
- Detecting the theme once and never listening again.
- Hiding focus rings in high contrast mode.
Verify:
- [ ] Dark tokens under prefers-color-scheme.
- [ ] forced-colors rules exist.
- [ ] The change listener is attached.
Output: theme.css, theme.js and the theme setting control.

examples.input: meu app desktop tem que seguir o tema escuro do sistema
examples.output: Tokens with prefers-color-scheme, System/Light/Dark setting, live listener, forced-colors rules
